requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is enabled on node1 and retains the intended policy after restart.
requirements.summary: Before restart, firewalld was active and enabled with matching runtime and permanent public-zone configuration. The acknowledged restart produced a connection interruption and a new boot ID; afterward the system, firewalld, and SSH recovered, and the same runtime and permanent firewall policy remained present. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

requirements.requirement: Inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 are permitted.
requirements.summary: Live nftables rules accept TCP/22 and TCP/8080. Bounded probes connected successfully to both ports before and after restart, with listener evidence confirming the TCP/8080 test endpoint and recovered SSH service.

The active and permanent public zone contain only SSH and TCP/8080 allowances with a REJECT target. TCP/9090 was confirmed listening yet rejected both before and after restart, and the live nftables input chain terminates in an explicit reject after the two allowed ports.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The sole managed node also has strong restart-protocol evidence: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement and observed interruption, a different post-restart identity corroborated by lifecycle collection, recovered system/firewalld/SSHD state, retained permanent configuration, and successful post-restart packet behavior.
limitations: Behavioral probes sampled IPv4 TCP ports 22, 8080, and 9090; rejection of other protocols and IPv6 traffic is supported by the observed inet firewalld/nftables policy rather than separate behavioral probes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The retained firewall change directly established the requested policy. The network namespaces, veth pairs, temporary listeners, PID files, and logs were bounded evidence fixtures and were removed. The first post-restart cleanup left the TCP/8080 listener running, but it was immediately diagnosed and removed; final lifecycle observations show no probe files or listeners, no failed services, and healthy package state. The restart was necessary for the provider protocol and persistence verification.
